annotation.cut_point:
We are given a **solid cube** with **side length 4 cm**, and it is cut into **two pieces** by a **plane** that passes through the **midpoints of six edges**.

We are to calculate the **surface area of each half-cube**, and round to the **nearest square centimeter**.

---

### **Step 1: Understand the cube**

- The cube has side length **4 cm**.
- Total surface area of the cube is:

$$
6 \times (4 \times 4) = 6 \times 16 = 96 \text{ cm}^2
$$

When we cut the cube into two pieces, the **total surface area** of the two pieces together will be:

$$
96 + 2 \times \text{(area of the new cut surface)}
$$

Because the cut introduces **two new faces** (one for each half-cube), each of which is a **square**.

The total surface area of the original cube is 96 cm^2.

The cut plane passes through the midpoints of six edges of the cube.
